sentences.text: Wellbore 15/9-F-15 C (Sodir wellbore 5794, purpose production, status P&A) has 84 daily reports from 2009-01-18 to 2013-11-10, and its first report without a before-spud flag is dated 2009-01-19.
The well duration is 1757.0 days, which includes the long gap between the end of section 11 on 2009-03-06 and the start of section 12 on 2013-10-06.
The deepest measured depth is 3232.0 m with a true vertical depth of 3044.0 m, and Sodir gives a total depth of 3232.0 m.
Total activity time is 1820.5 h, of which primary lost time is 421.25 h, a share of 23.14 % of the activity time.

Sodir gives an entry date of 2009-01-18 and a completion date of 2009-02-15; the completion date is the end of drilling, not production start-up, and the reports continue after it because the well was then completed, worked over and finally plugged and abandoned, with the last section of reports ending on the P&A status.

Section 1 has a hole size of 12.25 in and ran from 2009-01-18 to 2009-01-26, from 2575.0 m to 2920.0 m MD with 2748.0 m TVD at section end, drilling 345.0 m of new hole at 6.03 m/h (an average over all time coded drilling -- drill, not an on-bottom rate of penetration).

Section 2 has an unknown hole size (the reports do not state it) and ran from 2009-01-27 to 2009-02-06, with a start depth of 2971.0 m and an end depth of 2920.0 m MD as the tool reports them, 2748.0 m TVD at section end, no new hole and no time coded drilling -- drill, so no rate is available.

Section 3 has an unknown hole size (not stated in the reports) and ran from 2009-02-07 to 2009-02-08, from 2971.0 m to 2920.0 m MD as reported, 2748.0 m TVD at section end, with no new hole and no drilling rate.

Section 4 has an unknown hole size (not stated in the reports) and ran from 2009-02-09 to 2009-02-10, from 2971.0 m to 2920.0 m MD as reported, 2748.0 m TVD at section end, with no new hole and no drilling rate.

Section 5 has a hole size of 8.5 in and ran from 2009-02-11 to 2009-02-13, from 2920.0 m to 3232.0 m MD with 3044.0 m TVD at section end, drilling 312.0 m of new hole at 6.3 m/h (an average over all time coded drilling -- drill, not an on-bottom rate of penetration).

Section 6 has an unknown hole size (not stated) and ran from 2009-02-14 to 2009-02-15 at 3232.0 m MD and 3044.0 m TVD, with no new hole, so no rate is given even though 5.25 h are coded drilling -- drill.

Sections 7 to 10 are completion-phase sections with unknown hole size and no new hole: section 7 ran from 2009-02-16 to 2009-02-17, section 8 from 2009-02-18 to 2009-02-24, section 9 from 2009-02-25 to 2009-02-26 and section 10 from 2009-02-27 to 2009-03-03, all at 3232.0 m MD and 3044.0 m TVD at section end.

Section 11 is a workover-phase section with unknown hole size that ran from 2009-03-04 to 2009-03-06, from a reported start depth of 2971.0 m to an end depth of 3232.0 m MD, 3044.0 m TVD at section end and no new hole.
Section 12 (workover, unknown hole size, no new hole) ran from 2013-10-06 to 2013-10-11 and ended at 3232.0 m MD and 3044.0 m TVD.
Section 13 (workover, unknown hole size, no new hole) ran from 2013-10-12 to 2013-10-16 and ended at 3049.0 m MD; its true vertical depth is not reported.
Section 14 (plug and abandon, unknown hole size, no new hole) ran from 2013-10-17 to 2013-11-08 and ended at 3049.0 m MD with true vertical depth not reported.
Section 15 (plug and abandon, unknown hole size, no new hole) ran from 2013-11-09 to 2013-11-10 and ended at 1380.0 m MD with true vertical depth not reported.
Section 1 starts below a casing shoe at 2561.8 m MD and no casing was set during it.
Section 2 also starts below the 2561.8 m shoe and set casing with its shoe at 2914.8 m MD.
Sections 3, 4 and 5 start below the 2914.8 m shoe and set no casing.
Section 6 starts below the 2914.8 m shoe and set casing with its shoe at 3231.0 m MD.
Sections 7 to 13 start below the 3231.0 m shoe and set no casing.
Section 14 starts below the 2914.8 m shoe as the tool reports it and section 15 below a shoe at 1368.4 m MD; neither set casing.
Primary lost time over the wellbore is 421.25 h from 112 activities, which is 23.14 % of the 1820.5 h activity time.
By cause, primary lost time is 383.0 h of waiting on weather (81 activities), 34.5 h of repair (25 activities) and 3.75 h of fishing (6 activities).
By section, primary lost time in section 2 is 135.25 h, 56.35 % of that section's activity time, and in section 14 it is 262.0 h, 47.38 %; these two sections hold most of the primary lost time.
Section 15 has 12.5 h of primary lost time (32.89 %), section 9 has 4.75 h (9.9 %), section 12 has 5.5 h (4.17 %) and section 13 has 1.25 h (1.04 %).

Sections 1, 3, 5 and 7 have no primary lost time; the wait-on-weather time is coded as lost even though the reports show maintenance and some plug and tubing work done meanwhile, so it overstates pure idle time.

Possible lost time is reported separately and is not added to the primary figures: it totals 75.75 h from 43 activities, 4.16 % of the activity time, made up of 63.0 h coded interruption -- other, 11.75 h coded interruption -- maintain and 1.0 h coded drilling -- wait.
Possible lost time is largest in section 3 at 24.25 h (52.43 % of the section's activity time) and in section 1 at 21.25 h (12.57 %), both mostly rig-equipment troubleshooting.

On 2009-01-21 a surface mud-system fault (lost returns to the pit with falling standpipe pressure, traced to a blocked splitter valve in the suction module) cost 7.75 h in section 1; this is possible lost time, not primary.

On 2009-01-24 a 9 5/8-in casing joint was driven off the pipe-handler power rollers, and a safety time-out and investigation took 5.0 h of possible lost time; the practice was revised to one joint on the handler at a time.

From 2009-01-29 the rig waited on weather to run the production riser, a wait that continued until 2009-02-04 while maintenance was done; waiting on weather is the largest primary lost-time cause on the well at 383.0 h across the wellbore.
On 2009-02-06 the BOP connection pressure test failed repeatedly because the test plug leaked, costing 2.75 h of primary repair time.
On 2009-02-08 a hydraulic leak in the top-drive rotating head was troubleshot and repaired over 11.5 h (possible lost time), following a burst pipe-handler hose the day before.

On 2009-02-25 communication was found between the surface-controlled subsurface safety valve chambers in the communication collar and running tool, so seals were changed and a back-up running tool prepared, 3.75 h of primary repair time at 2796.0 m MD.
On 2013-10-10 a wireline toolstring parted at a time-delayed release and a fishing job followed; the fishing activities total 3.75 h of primary lost time.

On 2013-10-18 repeated attempts to release the adjustable-sub and running tool for the tie-back string failed, costing 2.75 h of primary repair time, and the same day the rig began waiting on weather to pull the production riser.
From 2013-10-30 the rig again waited on weather, this time to run the high-pressure drilling riser, and the wait continued to 2013-11-02; section 14 carries 262.0 h of primary lost time in total.

On 2013-11-07 a seal assembly hung up on the shear seal while run in the wellhead, and wellhead jet-washing, milling and repeated seal-assembly runs followed, giving section 15 primary lost time of 12.5 h.

The Sodir completion date of 2009-02-15 differs from the last report date of 2013-11-10 because the well was completed and worked over in the weeks after drilling ended, and then re-entered for a workover and plug and abandonment that reports from 2013-10-06 on.

Plan riser running and pulling inside a forecast weather window and keep productive work, such as plug retrieval, outside the waiting-on-weather code, because 383.0 h of primary lost time on this well is coded waiting on weather and it dominates sections 2 and 14.
Check the suction-module valves and pit line-up before drilling ahead, since the blocked splitter valve on 2009-01-21 took 7.75 h.
Keep the revised casing-handling practice of one joint on the pipe handler at a time, which followed the 5.0 h incident on 2009-01-24.

Surface-test the BOP test plug and the completion running tool, including the communication-collar seals, before running them, because the leaking test plug cost 2.75 h and the running-tool leak cost 3.75 h.
Review the wireline toolstring release mechanism and rig-up before jarring runs in tubing, since the parted toolstring left a fish and 3.75 h of primary fishing time.

Verify the wellhead seal profile and wear bushing condition, with a dummy run if needed, before the P&A seal-assembly runs, as the hang-up on 2013-11-07 led to 12.5 h of primary lost time in section 15.

Have the daily reports state the hole size and a consistent section depth for every section, since hole size is unknown for 13 of the 15 sections and the start depth of sections 2 to 4 is reported deeper than their end depth.

row.comments: Observed lost return to pit and falling standpipe pressure. Picked off bottom and reciprocated stand from 2827 m to 2841 m MD / 10 rpm.  No drop in active, annulus full, i.e. no downhole losses detected. Ivestigated situation. Inspected lines from pit to TDS, found no leakages. Closed IBOP and attmepted to pump, found that problem was related to the surface system.

Lined up cement unit to circulate on well. Circulated in well at set intervalls using cement unit pumping at 1200 lpm / SPP 26 bar. Reciprocated stand and rotated 10 rpm. Monitoed well on trip tank when not pumping - well static. Performed troubleshooting on pumps and circulation system.

Found likely cause of problem to be blocked splitter valve in suction module. Not able to use pit#7 as active pit. Lined up to pump from pit #15 taking retuns to pit #15 and #7 and used mixpump for levelling the two pits. Stepped up pumprate to 3400 lpm and RIH to 2853 m MD.

Held time out for safety and troubleshoting after a 9 5/8" casing joint was driven off of the HTS power rollers. Made up and ran 9 5/8" casing joint on HTS, installed swadge and kelly cock. Investigated incident. The 9 5/8" was tilted resting on the roller frame and the deck. The area in which the casing joint tilted was barriered off according to standard procedure for running HTS/PDM. Revised practice for picking up casing until further notice, i.e. only one joint on HTS rollers and HTS at the time.

Waited on weather to run production riser.

Meanwhile :
-Brought thension cylinders to Centralizer deck
-Replaced tension cylinders
-Changed wire on drillfoor yellow and black tugger
-Trobleshot HTS - no clear fault indication - random behaviour at w.r.t. stop point
-Performed maintenance of drawwork
-Emptied pit #5 into skips

Waited on weather to run production riser. Informed Production to shut down F-4, F-5 and F-14 at 01:35 hrs.

Meanwhile :
-Performed 5-yearly maintenance on standpipe manifold; C8
-Cleaned lower shakers
-Recovered moonpool 10 MT tugger from seabed
-Held tool box meeting for untangeling guide wires and running PR

Attempted to pressure test all connection between multibowl and BOP to 35 bar/5 min. No go. Opened lower pipe ram and closed middle pipe ram. Re-tested. No go. Re-sat test plug. No go, due to test plug was leaking.

POOH with test plug. No damage seen on test plug. MU, RIH and landed back-up test plug. Filled pipe with SW. Attempted to pressure test all connections between multibowl and BOP to 35 bar/5 min. No go, due to test plug was leaking.

Meanwhile RD broken tension cylinder on F-15.

Continued trouble shooting hydraulic leak in TDS rotating head. LO 10 3/4" tie-back csg onto HTS, removed PS21's, bails and elevator to have acess to TDS.

Meanwhile continued changing hydraulic tension cylinders on F-15 on centralizer deck. Performed housekeeping and maintenance.
Investigated problem. Found indication of communication between the ASV and DHSV chambers in the communication collar and running tool.
Disconnected control lines from running tool. Laid out primary running tool. Changed out seals on communication collar. Prepared back up running tool.
POOH from 284 m to surface. Toolstring parted at time delayed release below cable head.
Attempted to release adjustable sub tool several times. No success.
Pressured up string to 140 bar to work tool pistons. M/U tieback string w/ 5 right hand turns. Attempted to release DQ tool w/o success.
Attempted to release DQ tool on surface w/o success.

Waited on weather.

Meanwhile:
Cleaned and tidied wellhead deck and drill floor.
Performed planned maintenance.
Cleaned BOP's prior to pressure test.
Installed BOP test mandrel.

Waited on weather to run HPDR.

Meanwhile:
Performed planned maintenance and general housekeeping.
At 03:00 hrs informed Production to shut down according to yellow SIMOPS procedure.

Picked up seal assembly RT with "used" seal assembly (White painted).
RIH with seal assembly to below BOP.
POOH with seal assembly and inspected same, no damage observed.
RIH with seal assembly to 137 meter, hang up on shear seal, sat down 12 Ton.
